chief_complaint: new tiny red spots on my legs and heavy bleeding from gums
hpi_details: 35F presents with sudden onset of a non-blanching pinpoint red rash (petechiae) on her lower legs. She noticed her gums bleeding profusely after brushing her teeth. She had a severe viral upper respiratory infection 2 weeks ago.
ideas: thinks she has a blood disorder

investigation_events.title: STAT thrombocytopenia results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT platelet count and smear are now available; bleeding precautions and urgent hematology involvement should not be delayed.

results.value: Marked thrombocytopenia with occasional large platelets; no schistocytes or blasts

core_concepts: ITP involves IgG antibodies targeting platelets for destruction in the spleen.
Presents with isolated severe thrombocytopenia (no anemia or leukopenia).
common_misconceptions: Assuming a coagulation factor defect (PT/aPTT will be normal in ITP).
dangerous_errors: Discharging a patient with severe thrombocytopenia (<10k) due to risk of intracranial hemorrhage.
management_principles: Corticosteroids, IVIG, hematology consult. Avoid NSAIDs and trauma.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 35F with sudden petechiae and gingival bleeding following a viral illness.
reference_soap.objective: Widespread petechiae on bilateral lower extremities. Blood in oral cavity. Hemodynamically stable.
reference_soap.plan: STAT CBC, peripheral smear. Avoid NSAIDs. Hematology consult for possible IVIG and steroids.

learning_objectives: Identify clinical signs of severe thrombocytopenia (petechiae, mucosal bleeding).

teaching.one_liner: Sudden onset of petechiae and mucosal bleeding following a viral infection, indicative of ITP.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the tiny red spots on your legs and the gum bleeding?
Have you had a cold, flu, or any other viral infection in the past few weeks?
Have you noticed any other unusual bruising, nosebleeds, or blood in your urine or stool?
Are you taking any new medications, aspirin, or blood thinners?
Have you had any severe headache, confusion, or vision changes?
